cases.prompt: A public API lets unauthenticated contractors upload attachments to a customer folder through an invitation token scoped to one company. Several contractors may share the same worksite IP through NAT. A release is due today and the team proposes a user-plus-company limiter even though this path has no authenticated user. Audit the design and provide the limiter keys, companion controls, limit-exhaustion behavior, and residual risks. Do not invent production values.
expectations: Uses the invitation or token as the narrowest accountable actor instead of requiring an authenticated user
Applies independent tenant and global ceilings where the exposure requires them
Treats IP as a secondary signal because legitimate users may share a network
Covers atomic admission, idempotency, real payload bounds, and explicit 429 versus limiter-outage behavior
forbidden: Uses IP as the only primary limiter key

cases.prompt: An offline mobile application stores user-authored voice reports. When connectivity returns, the API may answer 429 or temporary 503. The current worker deletes a report after five failed attempts. Under pressure to ship, the team proposes excluding those responses from the failure counter and retrying automatically forever. Define the client and server behavior, counters, limits, and tests. Do not invent production values.
expectations: Preserves the durable report on transient failures without consuming permanent-failure attempts
Bounds automatic transient retries by an evidenced attempt budget, time horizon, or both
Transitions to an explicit resumable paused state instead of deleting data or retrying forever
Requires stable idempotency and bounded server-side actor, tenant, global, payload, and processing controls
forbidden: Deletes user-authored data because a transient retry budget is exhausted
Invents retry counts, delays, horizons, or quotas

cases.prompt: A critical feature accepts voice notes and then runs transcription and AI structuring. The shared Redis limiter is unavailable during an important customer operation. Management asks the team to accept and store every note without limits while blocking only AI processing until Redis returns. Evaluate the proposal, define the required boundaries and user-visible behavior, and list decisive tests. Do not invent production values.
expectations: Rejects unlimited durable ingestion as an unbounded storage and recovery queue
Allows degraded acceptance only inside independently authoritative item, byte, age, and capacity budgets
Keeps costly processing fail-closed while preserving locally durable user data when server admission is unavailable
Requires atomic concurrency tests, real payload verification, idempotency, cleanup, and controlled backlog recovery
forbidden: Accepts unmetered storage because AI processing is paused
Uses the unavailable limiter as the only durable-ingress safety boundary
Invents capacity, retention, retry, or AI-spend values
